skills.name: rea-looksmaxxing
skills.description: Run the /rea-looksmaxxing play - reverse engineer how a creator gets paid (Clavicular is the worked example) from their most viral clips, then post that formula through your own accounts and funnel everyone who replies or DMs into your offer, in your voice. Use when someone says /rea-looksmaxxing, "how does <creator> get paid", "moneymaxx like <creator>", or wants a creator's viral formula turned into posts, replies and DMs. Builds on treg's web-access skill for the social data and on log's MCP tools for the accounts.
skills.summary: Finds a creator's most viral clips and the formula behind them, then posts it through your accounts and funnels the replies and DMs into your offer, in your voice.

skills.name: log-discord-channel-reply
skills.description: Answering someone in a Discord DM or group DM. A log play (docs/useCases/discord/channelReply.md): Answer what someone said to the account in a Discord DM or group DM, with words: a question about what the owner is building, a reply to something the owner posted. A group DM is a private chat of a few people with no server; a channel inside a server ("pennyserver #general") is a different place, read and answered differently, and is [serverReply](serverReply.md). The chat is read first, the answer is written from what was said there and what the owner has told you, gated like every send, and sent through the account's one session. No meme and no voice note (those are [memeReply](memeReply.md) and [voiceNote](../inbox/voiceNote.md)).
skills.summary: Answering someone in a Discord DM or group DM

skills.name: log-discord-cold-outbound
skills.description: First DMs from a Discord channel. A log play (docs/useCases/discord/coldOutbound.md): Start a conversation with someone the owner met in a server channel: someone who replied to him, argued with him or asked him something there. log opens the DM the way the app's Message button does and sends one message, gated like any other. When Discord won't let a stranger message them, log sends a friend request instead, and the message waits until they accept.
skills.summary: First DMs from a Discord channel

skills.name: log-discord-forum-posts
skills.description: Going through a Discord forum for posts worth answering. A log play (docs/useCases/discord/forumPosts.md): Find a forum in a server, list its posts, read the ones that look right, and tell the owner which are worth answering and why: someone asking for help with something the owner has built or knows, a question nobody answered yet, a problem log solves. This page reads and sends nothing; answering one is [serverReply](serverReply.md).
skills.summary: Going through a Discord forum for posts worth answering

skills.name: log-discord-group-chat-read
skills.description: Reading a Discord group chat without Twenty. A log play (docs/useCases/discord/groupChatRead.md): Catch up on what was said in a Discord group DM over the last few hours, on the account's own session, with the account kept in a local file instead of Twenty. This page reads and sends nothing. A channel inside a server is read the same way by `"<server> #<channel>"`, but always live from Discord, since log.db keeps only its mentions and replies: see [serverReply](serverReply.md) for how a server channel differs from a group DM.
skills.summary: Reading a Discord group chat without Twenty

skills.name: log-discord-meme-reply
skills.description: Replying with a meme in a Discord chat. A log play (docs/useCases/discord/memeReply.md): Answer a moment in a Discord group or DM the way people there already do: with a meme. The chat is read first, [Memelord](https://www.memelord.com/sign-up?ref=kfwut9wc) finds a template that fits what was just said, the meme is gated like any other send, and it goes out as its media url, which Discord shows inline. Only Memelord's free tools are used (rule 41). The extension itself is described in [docs/extensions/memelord.md](../../extensions/memelord.md).
skills.summary: Replying with a meme in a Discord chat

skills.name: log-discord-server-reply
skills.description: Replying in a Discord server channel. A log play (docs/useCases/discord/serverReply.md): Answer someone in a channel of a Discord server: a mention of the account, a reply to its message, or a question in a channel the owner is part of, like "pennyserver #general". A server channel is not a group chat. It is a room inside someone else's server, with members who never joined a conversation with the owner, an owner and its own rules, so it is read, answered and sent differently from a DM or a group DM. DMs and group DMs are [channelReply](channelReply.md).
skills.summary: Replying in a Discord server channel

skills.name: log-discord-server-search
skills.description: Finding a conversation in a Discord server. A log play (docs/useCases/discord/serverSearch.md): Find what someone said in a server, or a conversation the owner had there, with Discord's own search across every channel, forum post and thread at once, then read around it. This is how "the conversation I had with <someone> about <a topic> in the <server> server" is found in one search instead of reading a channel back hundreds of messages. This page reads and sends nothing.
skills.summary: Finding a conversation in a Discord server

skills.name: log-facebook-groups
skills.description: Listening to local Facebook groups. A log play (docs/useCases/facebook/groups.md): The same accounts can join the local groups in their town and hear when someone asks for what the business sells ("anyone know someone who can take away an old sofa?"). This page shows the parts.
skills.summary: Listening to local Facebook groups

skills.name: log-facebook-marketplace-listings
skills.description: From accounts to live Marketplace listings. A log play (docs/useCases/facebook/marketplaceListings.md): How a local service business gets listings in front of people in every town it serves: take aged Facebook accounts, turn each one into a believable local profile, and post a listing from each one. This page walks one account all the way through, shows which part of log-cli does each step, and what decides that the step worked.
skills.summary: From accounts to live Marketplace listings

skills.name: log-inbox-boss-maxxing
skills.description: Bossmaxxing: giving out tasks to the team. A log play (docs/useCases/inbox/bossMaxxing.md): Give out tasks to the people the owner works with, wherever they are (a Discord group, an X DM, Slack, Instagram), and keep track of every job across the team: who has what, what they owe, what's blocked. Each task goes out as a brief that says what to do, why, what done looks like and by when. A live monitor stays on, so every reply is answered as it lands, and someone being set up is walked through one step at a time until it works.
skills.summary: Bossmaxxing: giving out tasks to the team

skills.name: log-inbox-governor-reset
skills.description: Resetting an account's governor count. A log play (docs/useCases/inbox/governorReset.md): Every platform account's governor counts what it sent today and refuses once the count is spent ("daily cap reached (500/day)"). When the owner says to, the count goes back to 0 so the work can carry on, on X, Discord, Slack, Instagram, Reddit, LinkedIn or Facebook alike. The reset is checked and kept in log.db, so it is never a hand edit nobody can see (rule 168).
skills.summary: Resetting an account's governor count

skills.name: log-inbox-ignore-server
skills.description: Ignoring a server or a chat. A log play (docs/useCases/inbox/ignoreServer.md): The live push brings every message that mentions, replies to or talks with the owner into his session. Some servers are only noise to him. When he says to ignore one, the push stops alerting on it: its messages are still heard and stored, readable any time, and DMs from the same people still come through. Undo lifts it.
skills.summary: Ignoring a server or a chat

skills.name: log-inbox-label-queue
skills.description: Teaching log who your people are. A log play (docs/useCases/inbox/labelQueue.md): log reads who each person is and where they are on every new message, with a small model on this machine. It is only as good as the labels it learns from, so it asks the owner about the chats it is least sure of, about ten minutes of his time, then trains on his answers. SubQ can label the rest once, as a paid pass he approves after seeing the cost.
skills.summary: Teaching log who your people are

skills.name: log-inbox-outcomes
skills.description: Do people answer what log sends?. A log play (docs/useCases/inbox/outcomes.md): log reads every send in log.db and splits them into the ones log sent (a send record, a sent queue item, or a log send call at that moment) and the ones the owner typed himself. It then compares how often and how fast people answered each, and whether they moved on to a later stage, first raw and then matched to the same person at the same stage, so a warmer audience for either side doesn't decide it. Nothing is sent and nothing is written.
skills.summary: Do people answer what log sends?

skills.name: log-inbox-quiet-push
skills.description: Quieting the live push. A log play (docs/useCases/inbox/quietPush.md): The live push brings every new message into the owner's session the moment it lands. When the owner wants a break from it, the push goes quiet for as many minutes as he says: the watchers keep hearing and storing everything, nothing is pushed into any session until then, and what came in arrives as one batch when it ends.
skills.summary: Quieting the live push

skills.name: log-inbox-rea-looksmaxxing
skills.description: /rea-looksmaxxing: moneymaxx like a creator. A log play (docs/useCases/inbox/reaLooksmaxxing.md): Reverse engineer how a creator gets paid, then run the same play on your own accounts. [treg](https://treg.to/?ref=matthewdonse-aebsh) reads the social data (the creator's most viral clips, the clip farms reposting them, views and comments), the formula is decoded from what won, and log posts it through your accounts and funnels everyone who replies or DMs into your offer, every message checked against how you write. Clavicular is the worked example: 40 of his clips pulled, the top one at 8.44M views, a looksmaxxing program as the offer. The video and the page (`log.listeningkit.com/rea-looksmaxxing`) tell the same play.
skills.summary: /rea-looksmaxxing: moneymaxx like a creator

skills.name: log-inbox-reactions
skills.description: Reacting to a message. A log play (docs/useCases/inbox/reactions.md): React to someone's message with an emoji on X, Discord, Slack or Instagram, the way a person answers a moment without typing: a laugh at a joke, a fire on a win, a heart on good news. It goes through the platform's own engine and the account's one session, never the browser, and counts as a write (rule 8).
skills.summary: Reacting to a message

skills.name: log-inbox-said-by
skills.description: Someone's messages on every platform, found by name, newest first. A log play (docs/useCases/inbox/saidBy.md): Someone's messages on every platform, found by name, newest first. Made from a hand-rolled one-off with log tool scaffold (getGuide({ useCase: "log/toolFromOneOff" })), so it is a log tool from now on and the one-off is never written again.
skills.summary: Someone's messages on every platform, found by name, newest first

skills.name: log-inbox-scope-ajob
skills.description: Scoping a job out of someone in a DM. A log play (docs/useCases/inbox/scopeAJob.md): Someone offers the owner a job in a chat. Before any number, any promise or any handover, the job has to be known: what it actually is, what they already have, what is blocked, and what "done" means to them. This page is that, and the writing rules that make the questions actually go out as the owner.
skills.summary: Scoping a job out of someone in a DM

skills.name: log-inbox-show-me
skills.description: Showing it as a view: generative UI in the chat. A log play (docs/useCases/inbox/showMe.md): The owner wants to see something rather than read it. The agent builds a view for that one question (stats, charts, people, a page per person) and log draws it in the chat with the numbers read from log.db. It reads only and sends nothing. A question about one person gets that person; a question about the week gets the week.
skills.summary: Showing it as a view: generative UI in the chat

skills.name: log-inbox-sign-in
skills.description: Signing an account in: checking it, then the live browser. A log play (docs/useCases/inbox/signIn.md): An account's session has run out, or it was never signed in. The agent checks it through the platform's own answer, and when it needs a person, it opens the account's own browser for the owner to sign in. It is streamed into the chat as a live view, on the owner's own machine and from a remote runtime alike, the same one the console's Connections page opens. A streamed browser has no window or taskbar entry of its own: the stream is its only view. The agent never types a password; the owner does.
skills.summary: Signing an account in: checking it, then the live browser

skills.name: log-inbox-triage
skills.description: Triage: scoping someone's job and handing it to whoever does it. A log play (docs/useCases/inbox/triage.md): A person comes to the owner needing something built. The owner is the face of the work: the person on the other side deals with him and nobody else. Behind that, the work goes to whoever actually does it. This page is that route: read what the person needing it has said, get the scope out of them, and hand the whole thing to the person who will build it, as a brief, without ever telling either side about the other.
skills.summary: Triage: scoping someone's job and handing it to whoever does it

skills.name: log-inbox-voice-note
skills.description: Sending a voice note. A log play (docs/useCases/inbox/voiceNote.md): Send someone a voice note in the owner's own cloned voice, as the platform's own voice note, on Discord, Instagram or Slack. It is made from the owner's words by the voice provider ([Inworld](https://inworld.ai/signup?ref=FSNLMJ2H) by default, [Fish Audio](https://fish.audio/?aff=Q6W4DNSLJCSXG) too) and goes through the platform's engine and the account's one session, never the browser (rule 142). A voice note only goes out when the owner asks for one.
skills.summary: Sending a voice note

skills.name: log-inbox-warm-people
skills.description: Working the warm people in your dms. A log play (docs/useCases/inbox/warmPeople.md): The people already in the owner's dms are the easiest yes. Every one of them carries who they are (lead, client, partner, friend, community, bot) and, for a lead or client, where they are (new, warming, needFound, offered, callBooked, won, lost, goneQuiet), read by a small local model on every new message, plus the old label: warming, readyToAsk, askedWaiting, cold, skip, friend or client. A bot, friend or partner never gets a sales stage, and the owner's own label always wins. The agent pulls the readyToAsk leads, reads each chat, and drafts the ask in his words.
skills.summary: Working the warm people in your dms

skills.name: log-instagram-dm-reply
skills.description: Reading and answering an Instagram DM. A log play (docs/useCases/instagram/dmReply.md): Read what someone wrote to the account on Instagram and answer it in the owner's voice, with text or a meme, on the account's own session through vendor/instagrapi. No browser, ever.
skills.summary: Reading and answering an Instagram DM

skills.name: log-instagram-new-platform
skills.description: Bringing a new platform up, then vendoring its client. A log play (docs/useCases/instagram/newPlatform.md): Make a platform log-cli doesn't have yet, open it in the account's [AdsPower](https://www.adspower.com/share/pD25Iu) browser, sign in by hand, keep the session, read what its own client called with rea, then find the open-source client that speaks the same calls and vendor it so the platform works on the direct-API engine. Instagram was the first one done this way.
skills.summary: Bringing a new platform up, then vendoring its client

skills.name: log-linkedin-network
skills.description: Growing a LinkedIn network, and reading and answering its inbox. A log play (docs/useCases/linkedin/network.md): Invite the people LinkedIn suggests on My Network, slowly, and read and answer the account's conversations, from its own session with no browser.
skills.summary: Growing a LinkedIn network, and reading and answering its inbox

skills.name: log-linkedin-posts
skills.description: Posting on LinkedIn, liking or reposting, and taking a post down. A log play (docs/useCases/linkedin/posts.md): Post text, an image or mentions from the account's own session, like or repost someone's post, or delete one of the account's own posts, each the way LinkedIn's own web client does it, with no browser.
skills.summary: Posting on LinkedIn, liking or reposting, and taking a post down

skills.name: log-log-browser-move
skills.description: Moving accounts to another browser. A log play (docs/useCases/log/browserMove.md): AdsPower is deprecated and Camoufox is log's browser. The agent moves accounts off AdsPower (or between any two browsers) with their signed-in session, and only calls one moved when the platform says it is signed in.
skills.summary: Moving accounts to another browser

skills.name: log-log-local-models
skills.description: Local models. A log play (docs/useCases/log/localModels.md): See which local models this release pins and whether each is on this machine at that revision, and, with the owner's yes, fetch the missing ones: the judge's injection classifier, the meaning model behind search and the router, the image describer and the mouse planner.
skills.summary: Local models

skills.name: log-log-secret-store
skills.description: Secret store status. A log play (docs/useCases/log/secretStore.md): Read whether log's account sessions, login secrets and provider keys are sealed in log.db, and which files still hold any in plain text. It reads only: nothing is sealed, moved or printed by value. Sealing itself needs no step; log does it the next time it uses each secret (docs/security/encryptedStore.md).
skills.summary: Secret store status

skills.name: log-log-tool-from-one-off
skills.description: Turning a hand-rolled one-off into a log tool. A log play (docs/useCases/log/toolFromOneOff.md): When the agent reaches for a one-off to get or change data (a scratch script over log.db, a raw `sqlite3` query, a `curl` to a platform or a link, a `python -c` or `bun -e`), log has no tool for that job yet. The hook labels the call `readsData` or `actsOnData` with what it touched, counts it in log.db, and says so before or right after it runs. It never blocks: the agent may finish the one-off, then makes it a real command and MCP tool so it routes from then on. The owner isn't asked; the guide below is the whole procedure.
skills.summary: Turning a hand-rolled one-off into a log tool

skills.name: log-log-tool-health
skills.description: Tool health. A log play (docs/useCases/log/toolHealth.md): Read how log's own tools are doing from the calls log.db already stores: per tool its calls, failures, commonest failure code, p50 and p95, and last use, with three flags (unused, failing, stale guide mentions) and a fix for each. It reads only: it changes no code, file or guide, and the fixes are for the owner to choose.
skills.summary: Tool health

skills.name: log-log-update-log
skills.description: Update log. A log play (docs/useCases/log/updateLog.md): Check which log runs here and, with the owner's yes, update it to the newest release and pick up where it left off: the hook service, the account watchers and the open browsers come back after the install. Nothing installs without the owner's yes.
skills.summary: Update log

skills.name: log-network-relationship-machine
skills.description: Relationship state machine. A log play (docs/useCases/network/relationshipMachine.md): Where you stand with someone, drawn as a state machine in the stately look: the states a relationship moves through (new, follows you, talks to your followers, engaged with you, you reached out, in conversation), the moves between them (follow, like their post, reply, DM, intro, they replied), each labelled with the log tool that makes it. The person's real history from log.db is the path taken, timestamped; where it stands now is highlighted, and the next move is the outgoing transition. The same machine shows the route to someone through the people you know, and your whole network with a count in each state.
skills.summary: Relationship state machine

skills.name: log-network-who-to-talk-to
skills.description: Who to talk to next. A log play (docs/useCases/network/whoToTalkTo.md): Your network is everyone around your own accounts, each in a ring kept live from what the watchers store: 1 engaged with you (a one-to-one chat counts, a group doesn't), 2 talks to your followers or ring-1 people, 3 follows you, 4 known. Rings are per person: accounts the owner linked (`log people link`) count once, at their closest ring, with every account and the platform each tie came from. Ask for one platform alone or all of them. It needs no research files. An imported research folder adds each person's band (what they could be to you), fit and the leaders whose circles they are in. One query answers who to talk to next: the people one step from you whom you haven't talked to yet, ring 2 first. Each comes with why: their ring and its reason, the circles, who already connects you, and their last post. The ones y
skills.summary: Who to talk to next

skills.name: log-people-facts
skills.description: Person facts. A log play (docs/useCases/people/facts.md): log keeps what people said that stays true (their job, where they work, what they are building, what the owner promised them, money owed) as events in log.db, each with the exact message it came from. A draft that says a promise again is held by the voice gate as already promised, and the person card, the conversation card and the Relate graph show the current facts.
skills.summary: Person facts

skills.name: log-reddit-contributor-maxxing
skills.description: Contributor maxxing: finding talented builders through what they share. A log play (docs/useCases/reddit/contributorMaxxing.md): Find talented people who are into the same things as the owner, through the GitHub repos they post on Reddit. Read a subreddit's last few days through the owner's Reddit account, keep the posts that link to GitHub, and rank them. It reads only. It posts, votes and messages nothing.
skills.summary: Contributor maxxing: finding talented builders through what they share

skills.name: log-slack-dm-reply
skills.description: Reading and answering a Slack DM. A log play (docs/useCases/slack/dmReply.md): Read what someone wrote to the account on Slack and answer it in the owner's voice, on the account's own session, with no browser.
skills.summary: Reading and answering a Slack DM

skills.name: log-tiktok-post
skills.description: Posting a video on TikTok, and deleting it. A log play (docs/useCases/tiktok/post.md): Post one video on the account's TikTok with a caption, and delete one of its posts, on the direct-API engine with no browser: the calls TikTok Studio makes, sent the same way. The AdsPower browser flows are the fallback when TikTok refuses a direct call. TikTok's own answers decide each step.
skills.summary: Posting a video on TikTok, and deleting it

skills.name: log-twitter-affiliate-marketing
skills.description: Affiliate marketing through your DMs. A log play (docs/useCases/twitter/affiliateMarketing.md): You use a tool, you make content about it, and people message you about it. This page turns those conversations into affiliate income without sounding like a pitch: each person gets a reply about their own thread, an update on what you've built, and the tool with your affiliate credit only where it actually helps them. The other side of the page is the tool companies themselves: getting onto their partner, referral or creator program and booking the call.
skills.summary: Affiliate marketing through your DMs

skills.name: log-twitter-collab-maxxing
skills.description: Collab maxxing: turn open conversations into collabs. A log play (docs/useCases/twitter/collabMaxxing.md): Network maxing gets people talking to the owner. Collab maxxing turns those conversations into something you can work on together. Everything the owner builds is open source and he earns nothing from it. So the collab is the deal: he builds their system with them and makes content about doing it, they get the outcome, and they back the work. Money is the last thing in the conversation, never the first. It comes as a small ask once they're keen, or a retainer the owner prices himself.
skills.summary: Collab maxxing: turn open conversations into collabs

skills.name: log-twitter-dm-inbox
skills.description: Reading the DM inbox: who is waiting on you. A log play (docs/useCases/twitter/dmInbox.md): Read every DM conversation on the account and sort it into a pipeline: who is waiting on you and what they asked, who you're waiting on, and what to do next for each. It sends nothing and marks nothing read. Replies only go out after the owner says what to send.
skills.summary: Reading the DM inbox: who is waiting on you

skills.name: log-twitter-engagement-replies
skills.description: Answering the people who engaged with your posts. A log play (docs/useCases/twitter/engagementReplies.md): When one of your posts gets comments, the people who commented are the warmest people on X for you. There are two ways to follow up, both public replies:
skills.summary: Answering the people who engaged with your posts

skills.name: log-twitter-engager-dms
skills.description: DMing the people who liked or reposted your post. A log play (docs/useCases/twitter/engagerDms.md): A post that does well leaves hundreds of people who liked or reposted it and were never followed up. This page turns them into a short list the owner knows is worth it, writes each one a DM that opens on why they're on the list, and sends them through the queue as dms.
skills.summary: DMing the people who liked or reposted your post

skills.name: log-twitter-follow-ups
skills.description: Following up in your own voice. A log play (docs/useCases/twitter/followUps.md): Answer or follow up the people the owner picked, each in the owner's own voice, the way they write to that person. It's for warming a relationship as much as for a deal: say it was good to meet, ask for advice, take someone up on an offer, keep a door open. Nothing goes out until the owner has seen every draft and said yes.
skills.summary: Following up in your own voice

skills.name: log-twitter-followers
skills.description: Checking who really follows you. A log play (docs/useCases/twitter/followers.md): Before a slide, a page or a message says someone follows you (or that you follow them), check it live on X. Engaging with you isn't following you. This page reads it on the account's own session and sends nothing.
skills.summary: Checking who really follows you

skills.name: log-twitter-get-the-action
skills.description: Getting people to do the thing: retweet, like, try it. A log play (docs/useCases/twitter/getTheAction.md): The owner needs people to do one action for him: retweet a post, like it, try the tool. This page goes through everyone talking to him, tells him in plain words what each conversation is about, and gets each of them a message that answers what they said and asks for the action. All of it goes out through the account's one queue.
skills.summary: Getting people to do the thing: retweet, like, try it

skills.name: log-twitter-manager-maxxing
skills.description: Manager maxxing: the managers of the biggest Kick streamers. A log play (docs/useCases/twitter/managerMaxxing.md): The owner's go-to-market, from his post (https://x.com/xAccount/status/2118285429674017268): find the manager of every Kick streamer on X, reply to their posts for a few days, then send each one a first DM about using log and showing Clavicular's X. The pitch, once they're talking: if Claude Code explains the sponsor deals a streamer does, with tracked links, sign-up rates go up, which means more affiliate money. Letting AI use your social media increases your surface area of luck.
skills.summary: Manager maxxing: the managers of the biggest Kick streamers

skills.name: log-twitter-network-maxing
skills.description: Network maxing: grow the network, the niche map. A log play (docs/useCases/twitter/networkMaxing.md): The point is to expand the owner's network, and the network is his niche map: the people around the communities and creators in his niche, each with their role, whether they follow him, and how close they sit to him. Network maxing grows it, one real conversation at a time. Every conversation is about getting to know them and what they're doing: what they're building, how they work, what's going on for them. It is never about what the owner sells.
skills.summary: Network maxing: grow the network, the niche map

skills.name: log-twitter-niche-map-region
skills.description: A new region of the niche map, then outbound to it. A log play (docs/useCases/twitter/nicheMapRegion.md): The niche map is the owner's network ([networkMaxing.md](networkMaxing.md)). A region is one world added to it, for example the YC 2026 batches (the founders, their companies and the partners around them). The region's people go through the same niche map pipeline as everyone else: three months of who talks to them, everyone scored, bands set, and each person's closeness to the owner (ring 1 engaged with him, ring 2 talks to his followers, ring 3 follows him, ring 4 new). The outbound then goes to ring 2 first, the warmest people who haven't talked to him yet.
